text:
ravi: Started bring-up for maelstrom-embed-v3 on our standard onboarding suite. Quick summary: float baseline beats prod on en-wiki holdouts (R@1 +0.018) but int6 per-channel shows a small R@10 regression on long-tail multilingual queries. Artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/maelstrom/2026-03-21/ci-1789

emma: what do you mean by long-tail multilingual?

ravi: queries with >12 tokens in es/pt/ru subsets. R@10 drops by ~0.022 vs prod, R@1 mostly stable for en.

jordan: that's odd. int6 usually hurts short queries more. any quant clipping seen?

ravi: we observed a handful of vectors with clipped values after uniform quant scaling. Per-channel helped, but a handful of channels still saturate on long sequences.

nina: did you try per-channel scaling with dynamic range calibration (using 1e5 samples)?

ravi: yes. Calib set size matters. Using 100k samples reduced clipping and improved R@10 back by ~0.012. Calib path: s3://redwood-evals/maelstrom/calib/100k. Script used: `eval/quant_calib.py --model maelstrom --samples 100000 --mode per_channel`

emma: normalization after dequant — helpful? L2 vs RMS?

ravi: L2 norm after decode recovers ~0.007 R@10 on the worst subset. RMS normalization (scale by sqrt(mean(x^2))) gives similar gains; L2 slightly better for cosine retrieval. We run `python eval/compare.py --norm l2` during the sweep.

jordan: Can we add a quick clustered-sanity check? t-SNE + DBSCAN to see density shifts (n_jobs=8).

ravi: ran t-SNE(3000 sample) + DBSCAN: cluster counts comparable, but some small clusters (size <10) merged under int6. Silhouette: float 0.21 -> int6 0.18. Not dramatic but noticeable.

nina: How about measuring rank correlation on pairwise similarities? Spearman between float and int6 vectors?

ravi: Spearman rho = 0.96 overall; for long-tail multilingual subset rho = 0.88. So ordering preserved mostly except tail.

emma: any failing examples we should surface for PM/human review?

ravi: added 30 human-review pairs where recall shift is largest (R@10 false negatives). Link: s3://redwood-evals/maelstrom/reviews/top30.csv. Example: "How to file taxes in Brazil" matched to different doc after int6 quant; float matched correct doc (sim 0.74 -> int6 0.33).

jordan: suspicious; could be tokenization difference for pt/pt-BR locale? Which tokenizer tag?

ravi: tokenizer v4 (byte-level subword). Same as prod. No locale-specific normalization applied.

emma: ops note? staging preview?

deploy-bot: Preview deployment ready at /staging/maelstrom-v3/quant-int6 (tag q-int6-stg). Canary flag off by default.

nina: propose decision criteria: for int6 canary enable we require: 1) global R@1 >= prod R@1 - 0.002, 2) multilingual long-tail R@10 >= prod R@10 - 0.01 after post-quant L2 norm, 3) Spearman rho >= 0.92 on multilingual subset, 4) no more than 5% of clusters with size change > 50% in sample clustering.

jemma: typo — I think you mean emma, not jemma. Also +1 to criteria. Add human-review pass for top 50 regressions before enabling canary.

emma: I'll run a focused 200k-sample calib with per-channel + outlier clipping (0.995 quantile) and re-evaluate. Queue: ci-quant-1820.

ravi: great. I'll also try RMS scaling before L2 and include both in the decision note. Will push a 1-page summary to the repo path: evals/notes/maelstrom-int6-decision.md and attach the review csv.

jordan: if int6 fails thresholds, fallback plan?

nina: fallback: enable int8 per-channel (lower size win but safer) on dedicated pools, keep float for hosted. Also ship per-tenant rollout flags.

ravi: timeline: finish recalib + normalization experiments by EOD, decision note before tomorrow morning. pinging offline PM for review.

deploy-bot: Canary toggle created: canary/maelstrom/int6. Toggle is off. Only ops can flip.

emma: thanks all, will report when ci-quant-1820 finishes. :thumbsup:
